sample_unit: R-peak detection algorithms benchmarked across five PhysioNet ECG datasets
models_evaluated: 17 R-peak detection algorithms (traditional signal processing, machine learning, deep learning)

links.outcome: Cross-dataset generalization of ML/DL R-peak detectors trained on a single dataset
links.effect: Under strict cross-dataset generalization without target-domain adaptation, traditional signal processing methods gave more consistent overall performance than ML/DL models, showing a trade-off between peak performance on familiar data and performance under distribution shift.
links.quote: Our results reveal that under a strict cross-dataset generalization setting, in which ML and DL models were trained on a single dataset without any target-domain adaptation, traditional signal processing methods provided more consistent overall performance.

screen.reason: Evaluates 17 R-peak detection algorithms (including ML/DL) across multiple benchmark datasets to assess cross-dataset generalizability and robustness under noise, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
